initiatives.title: Referral Engine (CX-driven, opt-in)
initiatives.why: We're a premium, trust-based practice — referrals must be earned through experience, not bought (no MLM, no discounts; the segment isn't price-sensitive). A great end-to-end experience makes referral automatic.
initiatives.next: Intern compiling the high-ticket value list. When ready → Lu presents to GM → gate Elaine-as-caller → trigger calls.
initiatives.gate: Premium-positioning gate: rewards = goodwill (e.g. RM50 NGO food voucher per successful referral), never clinic discounts.
initiatives.timeline: Three stages: (1) CX so good referral is automatic → (2) the referral → (3) post-referral thank-you. Intern building list now.

initiatives.note: Box 1 = Customer Experience (pre/in/post-visit + physical space = #5). Box 2 = the referral. Box 3 = thank the referrer when their referral shows up + produces. NGO voucher = food money for them + goodwill/moral gain (clinic invests in an NGO).

initiatives.timeline: Quick win; prerequisite for referral attribution (#9) and the physio channel (#8).

initiatives.why: Doctors had NO contract at all, and the employee paperwork was 20 years old. Redraft the employment terms, refresh the handbook, and move doctors onto contractor agreements (not employees) so the classification, the locum mechanics and the procurement rules are all written down.
initiatives.next: Lydia's line-by-line review of the doctor contractor agreement (first cut + counsel cover memo are with her). Then: get Erincy's contract to PDF and signed.
initiatives.timeline: Major progress 14 Jul. All contract docs now organised under one tracker with a playbook and a controlled vocabulary. Doctor agreement first cut done → with counsel.

Terminology standard set: chairside role = Dental Surgery Assistant; contractor docs say practitioner / professional fees / invoicing — never employee or salary.

initiatives.title: Payroll — Bonus & Increment 2026
initiatives.why: The annual reward round is the single biggest discretionary cost decision of the year and the main retention lever on a team we cannot afford to lose. It is funded from reserves, not from the year’s earnings — so it has to be timed and framed deliberately.
initiatives.next: Hold the one-to-ones: pro-rate the under-1-year staff, and settle the two open individual cases.
initiatives.gate: Funded from reserves (2026 economic baseline is roughly break-even) — so the round is a deliberate draw, not a distribution of profit.
initiatives.timeline: ANNOUNCED 12 Jul by Dr Ong, framed on the 20th anniversary. One-month bonus PULLED FORWARD to July (paid with July salary); increment moved to YEAR END. One-to-ones follow.

tasks.t: 20-year payroll history + increment tracker rebuilt
Round designed: bonus forward to July, increment to year end
Announcement speech drafted + delivered by Dr Ong — 12 Jul
Pay the one-month bonus with July salary
One-to-ones: pro-rate staff under 1 year
Settle the two open individual cases
Year-end increment decision + payout

initiatives.note: Deliberate design: bonus early (cash goodwill now, when the team can feel it) and increment late (a permanent cost — hold it until the year is known). Announced at clinic level with "details one-to-one" as the safety valve, so no individual number was disclosed in the room. Individual figures stay off this board.

initiatives.title: Locum Compensation Redesign
initiatives.why: Two legacy carve-outs quietly cost the clinic real money every year: X-rays are not shared, and one doctor’s ortho work is exempt from the 10%. Together they are worth roughly RM63k/year — close to the cost of the front-desk and DSA headcount we actually need.
initiatives.next: Move the X-ray sharing policy first (universal, defensible now); phase the ortho change later, and land both through the new contractor agreement rather than a conversation.
initiatives.gate: Decouple the two: X-ray = a universal clinic policy applied to everyone; the ortho 10% = a single-doctor renegotiation, phased.
initiatives.timeline: Analysis done. X-ray policy now; ortho phased later. Both ride on the doctor contractor agreement (#16).

tasks.t: Quantify both carve-outs (X-ray ~RM35.8k/yr; ortho 10% ~RM27.4k/yr)
Legal framing agreed: the X-ray machine is a licensed clinic asset
Introduce X-ray sharing as universal policy
Phase the ortho 10% renegotiation
Write both into the contractor agreement / Schedule 1

initiatives.note: The framing matters more than the number: the X-ray unit is a licensed clinic asset (AELB licence sits with the clinic, not the practitioner), so sharing its revenue is a policy applied to everyone — not a cut to one person. That is why it goes first. ~RM63k/yr recovered ≈ funds the front-desk + DSA roles.
